evidence.text: [THE COMPANY] contractually committed, in its own communique, to give a status update on the strategic review of its Lockers business ON THIS RELEASE (23 September 2026) -- with Rothschild & Co, Societe Generale and Darrois Villey already mandated at launch -- and only part of the deal option is still in the price: the stock rose +6.00% on the 20 July announcement and peaked at EUR 13.68 on 3 August (+14.0% vs EUR 12.00 pre-announcement) but sits at EUR 12.46 today, so roughly two thirds of the peak premium has bled out ahead of the one date the company itself named.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is exactly one prior instance of this line and it is the launch itself: 2026-07-20, the stock closed +6.00% at EUR 12.72 on 96,222 shares against a 60-day median of 37,606 (2.6x), then drifted to EUR 13.68 by 3 August. The line has never been tested by an UPDATE, which is why my band is wide in both directions: the modal outcome is 'process continues, no decision', a signed or near-signed disposal is the fat right tail, and 'we will retain and invest' is the left tail. The path to the equity is stated rather than assumed: net debt was EUR 682m at 31 January 2026 at 3.0x leverage including leasing (1.6x excluding), against a EUR 429m market capitalisation on 34,468,912 shares, so a disposal near the EUR 180m French estimate cuts net debt by about a quarter and removes the balance-sheet overhang that French coverage names as the single biggest concern on the name.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partly priced and I size it as such -- the launch is English wire copy and the stock paid +6% for it. What is not in the price is the dated update. If the market were positioned for an outcome on 23 September, the stock would not have given back two thirds of its announcement premium into the one date the company named, and the 5-day run-up would not be +0.48% with the 20-day at -3.11%; a market anticipating a disposal announcement bids a EUR 429m equity ahead of a EUR 180m asset decision rather than drifting from EUR 13.40 on 4 September to EUR 12.26 on 18 September. The AMF short register does not name the issuer, so there is no crowded short being squeezed and no positioning tell either way. With 5 analysts covering a name trading $0.5m a day, there is also no preview machine to put a probability-weighted disposal into the price the way there would be at 16-19 analysts.
evidence.independence: Two independent corroborations. (1) Sector context from a different publisher: Axios Pro reported the same day that the review 'follows FedEx and Advent's $9.2 billion bid for European locker firm InPost', i.e. the European locker sector has an active strategic bidder -- [url removed] (2026-07-20). (2) An independent French sizing of the asset, DR Bourse 2026-07-21: 'Sur une valorisation de 15x l'EBITDA, l'activite Lockers pourrait etre cedee pour 180 M EUR' [At a 15x EBITDA valuation, the Lockers business could be sold for EUR 180m] -- [url removed] . EUR 180m is 42% of the EUR 429m market capitalisation. NOTE THE DEPENDENCE WITH FINDING 4: finding 4 is a haircut on this finding's upside (the asset is trading worse than the sale narrative), not an independent negative, and this finding is sized well below the full option value partly for that reason.

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY] voluntarily pre-disclosed a strongly positive operational datapoint about the quarter being reported -- Digital global bookings up more than 20% year on year like-for-like in Q2, with French e-invoicing bookings up more than ten-fold -- four weeks before the print and before the quiet period opened, which materially lowers the probability of the FY2026 guidance cut that is this stock's only demonstrated -15% trigger.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is the whole reaction function on this name and it is cleanly measured over three events. FY2025 guidance CUT at the H1 2025 print (filed 2025-09-24 after the close; 'FY 2025 revenue is now expected to decline by a low single digit on an organic basis', replacing 'acceleration in organic revenue growth') -> EUR 15.94 to EUR 13.10, -17.82%. FY2025 results with a EUR 124m Mail goodwill impairment (filed 2026-03-25 after the close) -> EUR 12.68 to EUR 10.88, -14.20%. FY2026 guidance CONFIRMED at Q1 (filed 2026-05-21 after the close) -> EUR 11.98 to EUR 12.34, +3.01%. So this stock pays roughly +3% for a confirmation and roughly -15% for a cut: sharply asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the reason my emitted move is far below the upside of my band.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partially priced -- the stock rose +3.26% on 92,795 shares (2.5x the 60-day median) on 24 August -- and then the whole of that move was given back: EUR 13.18 on 31 August to EUR 12.46 today, -5.5%. So the market bought the datapoint and then sold the print risk. What is NOT priced is its function as a negative signal about a guidance cut: managements four weeks from cutting a full-year guide do not usually publish '+20% bookings growth' under their own name. If the market had read it that way, the pre-print drift would not have been -8.5% from EUR 13.40 on 4 September to EUR 12.26 on 18 September. The French-language version of the same release exists in the AMF flux, so this is not a language gap -- it is an attention gap on a 5-analyst name, and the release was categorised 001006 (ordinary communique), not as regulated results information, which is exactly the classification that defeats a headline filter.
evidence.independence: Corroborated by a different document and a different metric: the Q1 2026 release reports Digital annual recurring revenue of EUR 257m at end-Q1, +15.9% annualised organic -- [url removed] (2026-05-21). And independently, the structural driver went live inside the reporting gap: [THE COMPANY] filed on 2026-09-01 that it and its partners 'Support More Than 800,000 Entities as France's First Phase of E-Invoicing Reform Takes Effect', with Serensia by [THE COMPANY] definitively approved by the DGFiP -- AMF flux record, PDF at [url removed] (2026-09-01). Note the shared-document caveat with finding 4: both touch the 21 May Q1 release, but this finding's load is carried by the 24 August document.

evidence.text: The AMF published a 'franchissement de seuils' on [THE COMPANY] on 21 September 2026 -- two days before the print, in French only, with no English wire version -- whose headline (a holder crossing DOWN through 5%) reads far more negative than the arithmetic inside it: Janus Henderson Investors UK sold only 32,062 shares, 1.8% of its holding, and still holds 1,709,808 shares or 4.96%, having crossed UP through 5% on 23 July by buying on market three sessions after the Lockers review was announced.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measurable on this name: the AMF short register has never named [THE COMPANY] (anchor_covered false, register_read_no_position), so there is no disclosed-short history to read a squeeze or a cover off, and threshold declarations on a EUR 429m small cap do not normally carry a same-week price signature. evidence.why_not_priced: It exists only in the AMF's French declaration archive and in no English wire, no broker note and no aggregator I could reach. If the market had read it, a 'largest disclosed holder cuts below 5% two days before results' headline on a EUR 429m name would have shown up as a down day on elevated volume on 21 or 22 September; instead the stock traded +1.14% on 50,186 shares and +0.48% on 14,420 shares, the latter being 38% of the 60-day median volume -- the two quietest sessions of the month. evidence.independence: The two paired declarations are separate AMF filings by the same declarant and I am treating them as ONE finding, not two. evidence.text: The asset being put up for review is trading badly on the line a buyer pays for: [THE COMPANY]'s own Q1 2026 release discloses that Lockers non-recurring revenue fell 44.6% organically, taking the whole Lockers segment to -3.8% organic after +11.2% in H1 2025, and French coverage explicitly names this as the concern hanging over the 23 September checkpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The market has already been shown this exact number once and looked straight through it: the -44.6% was disclosed in the 21 May 2026 Q1 release and the stock rose +3.01% the next session, because subscription revenue in the same segment grew 18% organically and is now 80% of Lockers revenue against two thirds in FY2025. That is the single strongest argument for sizing this small, and it is why I cut it rather than carrying it at a full point. Its live bite is narrower: the FY2026 guide contains an explicit 'EBITDA margin above 10% in Lockers' target, up from 5.0% in FY2025, and a second weak hardware quarter puts that specific line at risk on a name that pays roughly -15% for a guidance cut.
evidence.why_not_priced: The number itself IS priced -- it was in the May release and the stock went up. I have deliberately NOT sized that reframing as new information about the quarter; I have sized it as a haircut on finding 1. If the market had already applied that haircut, the stock would not still be carrying +3.8% of the July announcement premium.
evidence.independence: The -44.6% is confirmed in the primary company document, which is what makes it usable at all rather than a secondary claim: 'Lockers revenue amounted to EUR 24 million in first-quarter 2026, down 3.8% on an organic basis', with non-recurring revenue down 44.6% organically and subscription-related revenue up 18% -- [url removed] (2026-05-21). NOT INDEPENDENT OF FINDING 1: this is the offsetting side of the same asset and I have netted it rather than counting it twice -- finding 1 is [sizing note removed].5 against a French estimate of EUR 180m (42% of market cap) precisely because this exists.

evidence.text: The actual announcement, signing or completion of a Lockers transaction, as opposed to a status update. evidence.text: The FY2026/2027 outlook given on 23 September has to lap three things that do not repeat: a ~EUR 30m one-off from the sale of licensing rights tied to the North American corn divestiture, a EUR 7.7m participation gain from selling the AgReliant JV stakes, and the AgReliant equity income itself - on top of a Russian business [THE COMPANY] says is still shrinking. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is where this stock's biggest moves have come from. 2026-02-12, comparable sales guidance cut from ~3% to flat with the margin band held: -7.42%. 2025-02-13, the equivalent H1 guidance event a year earlier: -9.49%. 2025-09-25, FY24/25 results setting the 3% FY25/26 guide plus the new three-year 3-5% / 19-21% medium-term frame: -3.13%. All three negative, and the two that changed a number were the two largest.
evidence.why_not_priced: The English-language record carries the EUR 29m one-off as a line in the 9M release but not the second item - the EUR 7.7m participation gain - and nowhere joins them to the FY26/27 base. The AgReliant divestiture ad-hoc of 2025-06-27 quantified the proceeds only as 'a low three-digit million range (USD)'; there is no public number for the equity income [THE COMPANY] loses with it. With five analysts and no published note since 20.07.2026, nobody has walked the market through an FY26/27 EBITDA base that is roughly EUR 30m lower before a single operating assumption is made. If this were priced, the stock would not be trading 2.6% off its high into the release, and the July target raise (78->85) would have been accompanied by a cut to FY26/27 estimates.

evidence.text: The 2027 German sugarbeet contracting round is already settled and it came out BETTER than the two preceding years, which [THE COMPANY] can underwrite in its FY26/27 outlook: the SZVG - the growers' cooperative that holds the majority stake in Suedzucker - has released 100% of delivery rights for the 2027 cultivation contract, cancelling the 90% restriction imposed in spring, explicitly because of the expected fall in sugar output from the 2026 harvest. Sugarbeet is EUR 324.6m of [THE COMPANY]'s EUR 386.8m 9M group EBITDA, and European beet seed is billed in the Jan-Mar quarter that sits inside FY26/27.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent: [THE COMPANY] has guided European beet acreage DOWN at each of its last three releases and the stock fell each time (-3.13%, -7.42%, -2.31%). There is no observation in the last two years of [THE COMPANY] guiding beet area up, so this is the first time the segment narrative could turn and the reaction is unmodelled - which is the argument for a real but bounded positive rather than a large one.
evidence.why_not_priced: The English-language coverage of EU sugar in August and September 2026 is entirely about the PRICE and the CROP - NW European sugar at EUR 550/t on 3 September, +40% year to date, EU 2026/27 output cut to a 38-year low - and says nothing about the contracting decisions that actually set how much beet seed [THE COMPANY] sells. Those decisions live on a German growers' cooperative website and in the German farm press, in German, and they are the transmission mechanism. If the market had read them, the sell-side would have a published FY26/27 European beet-volume assumption, and there is no note on the name since 20.07.2026. Sized small deliberately, for three reasons the same German sources give: the SZVG decision covers southern Germany only, a fraction of [THE COMPANY]'s global beet seed book; Nordzucker's agreed 2027 minimum price is EUR 31.00/t, below prior years; and Pfeifer & Langen has cut more than 80 growers with ~1,200 ha out of 2027 contracts altogether. This is a direct counterparty in the beet chain speaking, not [THE COMPANY], so it is a hypothesis about [THE COMPANY]'s guidance until [THE COMPANY] says it.
